concepts.name: Classification and Typology of Droughts
key_dimensions: Four types: Meteorological, Hydrological, Agricultural, and Socioeconomic drought — definitions and distinctions
UPSC trap: Meteorological drought does NOT always lead to agricultural drought (soil moisture buffering)
Ecological drought as an emerging fifth category — biodiversity and ecosystem stress
Sequential relationship: how one type triggers another and the time-lag involved

concepts.name: IMD's Criteria for Declaring Meteorological Drought
key_dimensions: Deficiency of 26–50% of normal rainfall = 'Drought'; >50% deficiency = 'Severe Drought'
UPSC trap: Drought declaration is based on departure from Long Period Average (LPA), not absolute rainfall amount
District-level vs. sub-divisional level drought declaration — administrative implications
Distinction between 'drought year' and 'drought-affected area' — India may have drought pockets even in a normal monsoon year

concepts.name: Spatial Distribution of Drought-Prone Regions in India
key_dimensions: Chronically drought-prone states: Rajasthan, Gujarat, Maharashtra (Marathwada/Vidarbha), Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Odisha
UPSC trap: Northeast India and Western Ghats windward side rarely face droughts despite being 'extreme' rainfall zones
Peninsular India's unique vulnerability — hard-rock Deccan terrain limits groundwater recharge
Drought Atlas of India (NRAA) — identification of 188 drought-prone districts covering ~33% of India's geographical area

concepts.name: Causes of Droughts in India: Climatic and Non-Climatic Factors
key_dimensions: El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO): positive correlation between El Niño years and Indian drought incidence
Weak or failed southwest monsoon as the primary trigger — role of Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD) as a moderating factor
Anthropogenic factors: deforestation, overextraction of groundwater, land-use change increasing drought intensity
UPSC trap: Not all El Niño years produce droughts (e.g., 1997 El Niño did not cause severe Indian drought) — IOD offset

concepts.name: El Niño and Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD): Interaction with Indian Monsoon and Drought
key_dimensions: El Niño weakens Walker Circulation → suppresses southwest monsoon → drought risk
Positive IOD can neutralize El Niño's negative impact on Indian rainfall — 2019 example
UPSC trap: La Niña generally favors above-normal monsoon but is NOT a guarantee against regional droughts
Madden-Julian Oscillation (MJO) as a short-term modulator — active/break phases of monsoon

concepts.name: Drought Monitoring Mechanisms and Indices in India
key_dimensions: Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI): most widely used — measures precipitation anomaly over multiple timescales
Palmer Drought Severity Index (PDSI): incorporates temperature and soil moisture — used for agricultural drought
NDVI (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index) from satellites — used by ISRO/NRSC for real-time drought monitoring
UPSC trap: SPI uses only precipitation; PDSI is more comprehensive but computationally complex — IMD uses SPI primarily

concepts.name: Drought-Prone Area Programme (DPAP) and Desert Development Programme (DDP)
key_dimensions: DPAP (1973): targets chronically drought-prone areas — watershed development as core strategy; covers 972 blocks in 182 districts
DDP (1977–78): targets hot arid zones (Rajasthan, Gujarat, Haryana) and cold arid zones (Ladakh) — distinct from DPAP
UPSC trap: DPAP and DDP were merged into the Integrated Watershed Management Programme (IWMP) in 2009, later into PMKSY-WDC
Watershed as the planning unit — shift from relief-centric to development-centric approach

concepts.name: National Disaster Management Framework for Drought: Legal and Institutional Aspects
key_dimensions: UPSC trap: Drought is NOT notified as a 'disaster' under the Disaster Management Act, 2005 — it is managed under the Manual for Drought Management (2016) by MoAFW
State governments declare drought (not Centre) — based on IMD data, crop loss surveys, and groundwater levels
SDRF and NDRF fund flow mechanism — drought relief norms and conditionalities
Four-phase drought management cycle: Early Warning → Declaration → Relief → Recovery

concepts.name: Manual for Drought Management (2016): Key Provisions
key_dimensions: Replaces 2009 guidelines — introduces four drought indicators: rainfall, remote sensing (NDVI), agriculture (crop sowing), and hydrology (groundwater/reservoir levels)
Three-tier declaration: Sub-district (Taluka/Mandal) → District → State — minimum two indicators must show stress
UPSC trap: A state can declare drought even if IMD classifies monsoon as 'normal' at the national level — regional variation matters
Emphasis on 'do more with less water' — demand-side management over supply augmentation

concepts.name: Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) and Drought Mitigation
key_dimensions: 'Har Khet Ko Paani' and 'More Crop Per Drop' — two core pillars addressing water access and efficiency
PMKSY-WDC (Watershed Development Component) — successor to IWMP — treats watersheds as drought-proofing units
UPSC trap: PMKSY is an umbrella scheme merging AIBP (Accelerated Irrigation Benefits Programme), IWMP, and On-Farm Water Management — not a new standalone scheme
Micro-irrigation (drip/sprinkler) promotion under PMKSY — reduces water demand and drought vulnerability

concepts.name: Groundwater Depletion and Its Relationship with Agricultural Drought
key_dimensions: Over-extraction of groundwater for irrigation during droughts creates a 'drought trap' — worsening future drought resilience
Hard-rock Deccan terrain (Peninsular India) — low aquifer storage capacity intensifies agricultural drought even after normal rainfall
UPSC trap: States with highest groundwater extraction (Punjab, Haryana) are LESS drought-prone meteorologically but face water stress due to overuse
Atal Bhujal Yojana (2020) — community-led groundwater management in 7 drought-prone states

concepts.name: Drought and Food Security: Impact on Agriculture and Farmers
key_dimensions: Kharif crops (rice, cotton, pulses) are most vulnerable to monsoon failure — direct link to drought-induced food inflation
UPSC trap: Rabi crops are NOT immune — delayed or weak northeast monsoon affects rabi water availability in southern India
Farmer distress and agrarian crisis — Marathwada drought belt and farmer suicide nexus (sociological dimension)
Buffer stock norms and food grain release policy as drought-response instruments — role of FCI

concepts.name: Traditional Water Conservation Systems as Drought-Coping Mechanisms
key_dimensions: Rajasthan: Johads, Kunds, Tankas, Baoris — community-managed rainwater harvesting in Thar Desert
Tamil Nadu: Eris (tank irrigation system) — sequential tank cascades for drought buffering in rain-shadow zones
UPSC trap: These systems are NOT just historical — SC in Rajasthan High Court cases has recognized revival of johads as a legal right to water
Apatani system (Arunachal Pradesh) and Zabo system (Nagaland) — contrast with arid zone systems to show geographic diversity

concepts.name: Drought and Climate Change: Projected Trends for India
key_dimensions: IPCC AR6 (2021): India likely to face increased frequency of flash droughts (rapid onset within weeks) due to rising temperatures increasing evapotranspiration
Warming reduces soil moisture even when rainfall is 'normal' — temperature-driven drought decoupled from precipitation
UPSC trap: Climate change may increase BOTH extreme rainfall events AND droughts simultaneously in India — not a paradox but a sign of increased variability
Western Ghats rain-shadow areas and central India identified as emerging drought hotspots by NATCOM reports

concepts.name: Interlinking of Rivers (ILR) as a Drought Solution: Merits and Criticisms
key_dimensions: National Water Development Agency (NWDA) — Himalayan and Peninsular components of ILR — designed to transfer water from surplus to deficit basins
Ken-Betwa Link Project (first ILR project): transfers water from Ken (surplus) to Betwa (drought-prone Bundelkhand) — Madhya Pradesh and UP
UPSC trap: ILR addresses hydrological drought but may worsen ecological drought — threatens Panna Tiger Reserve ecosystem
Arguments against ILR: high cost, displacement, disruption of river ecology, and questionable surplus basin assessment — Mihir Shah Committee critique

concepts.name: Bundelkhand as a Case Study of Chronic Drought and Policy Response
key_dimensions: Geological factor: Bundelkhand craton (ancient hard rock) — extremely poor groundwater recharge despite being in sub-humid zone
Social dimension: drought → distress migration → abandonment of traditional water harvesting (ponds, bundhs)
Special Bundelkhand Package (2009) and its limitations — infrastructure focus over livelihood drought-proofing
UPSC trap: Bundelkhand spans TWO states (MP and UP) — inter-state coordination challenge in drought management and the Ken-Betwa project

concepts.name: Flash Drought: Concept, Causes, and India's Vulnerability
key_dimensions: Definition: Rapid onset drought developing over weeks (not months) due to sudden rainfall deficit + high temperatures + strong winds
Different from conventional drought in monitoring challenge — traditional indices (SPI) have poor early warning for flash droughts
UPSC trap: Flash droughts are increasingly associated with climate change in India but are DISTINCT from heat waves — though co-occurring
Central and Peninsular India most vulnerable — 2009 and 2015 kharif seasons showed flash drought characteristics

concepts.name: Drought Relief Norms under SDRF/NDRF: Financial Mechanisms
key_dimensions: SDRF (State Disaster Response Fund): primary fund for disaster relief — Centre contributes 75% (90% for NE/hilly states); States contribute 25%
NDRF activated only when state resources are inadequate — Inter-Ministerial Central Team (IMCT) assesses state's drought relief request
UPSC trap: Drought relief norms were revised in 2015 (14th Finance Commission period) — input subsidy to farmers replaced by direct DBT-linked relief in many states
Compensation norms: 33% crop loss threshold required for relief; >50% loss attracts higher compensation — these thresholds are frequently tested

concepts.name: National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC) and Drought Resilience
key_dimensions: National Water Mission (NWM) — one of 8 NAPCC missions — targets 20% improvement in water use efficiency; directly addresses drought vulnerability
National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA) — drought-resistant crop varieties, soil health, and contingency crop planning
UPSC trap: NAPCC does NOT have a dedicated 'Drought Mission' — drought is addressed across NWM, NMSA, and National Mission for Green India (NMI) — cross-mission nature
State Action Plans on Climate Change (SAPCC) — states like Rajasthan and Maharashtra have drought-specific adaptation strategies under SAPCC

concepts.name: Drought Vulnerability Index and Composite Risk Assessment
key_dimensions: Vulnerability = Exposure × Sensitivity ÷ Adaptive Capacity — districts with high exposure but high adaptive capacity (irrigation, income) have lower vulnerability
NRAA (National Rainfed Area Authority) Drought Vulnerability Atlas — ranks districts on composite index combining physical and socioeconomic parameters
UPSC trap: High rainfall variability (CV > 30%) is a better drought risk indicator than average annual rainfall — Rajasthan and Vidarbha both have high CV despite different rainfall totals
Gender and caste dimension of drought vulnerability — women and marginal farmers bear disproportionate drought burden — relevant for GS-I social geography angle
